Definition: from G4314 and G5342 (including its alternate); to bear towards, i.e. lead to, tender (especially to God), treat:--bring (to, unto), deal with, do, offer (unto, up), present unto, put to.
BiblicalUsage: Prosphero means to bear toward, to bring and present, especially to offer to God. Every high priest is ordained to offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins, but Christ offered Himself without spot to God, and then sat down on the right hand of God, because one sacrifice had done what thousands could not. The wise men opened their treasures and presented unto Him gifts, gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe offering is the motion of worship: men bring gifts to God, priests bring sacrifices, and Christ brought Himself. I hold that no offering I bring can stand beside His, because His was the only one God ever needed, and it was offered once for all.
